answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a stake that is locked before an identity earns voting weight. For each new identity, the operator must post a bond; votes are weighted by that bond, and provable double-signing forfeits it. Splitting the same stake among a thousand names does not multiply influence, while buying more requires more capital and exposes it to loss. An ivory kernel may route falcon messages, but it cannot make one bond count as many.
